data.body:
S0 ADR DRAFTED (uncommitted) — docs/adr/0111-on-box-disk-ceiling-architecture.md, 257 lines, plus .numbers/0111 and a one-line README index entry. All gates green: check_docs_index rc=0, check_adr_numbers rc=0, gen_adr_index --check rc=0, make lint rc=0, 27 tests passed.

## FOUR corrections to what I briefed — record these, two matter beyond this story

1. **ADR 0110 was already taken.** docs/adr/0110-change-shape-advisory-not-blocking.md landed on origin/main in commit 8f19115cf2fb (2026-09-01), AFTER the epic was planned. The story's plan asserted "highest current number is 0109" and the plan-review gate BLOCKED on exactly that. Corrected to 0111 everywhere. Reusable lesson: a plan that pins an ADR number at authoring time goes stale silently, because other work allocates numbers meanwhile. The gate caught it only because it RE-DERIVED the fact instead of trusting the plan's assertion.

2. **The slug had to change too, for a non-obvious reason.** gen_adr_index.py buckets ADRs by FIRST-MATCHING KEYWORD in slug order, and "gerrit" is claimed by the earlier "Git / Gerrit workflow" group — so 0110-gerrit-disk-ceiling-... would have filed an INFRA adr under Gerrit workflow. Renamed to 0111-on-box-disk-ceiling-architecture ("on-box" is an Infra & deploy keyword, alongside 0079/0104/0105). Verified it renders under Infra & deploy.

3. **I OVERSTATED the no-upsize constraint, repeatedly, including to the operator.** I had been saying "ADR 0079 and 0104 explicitly decided against upsizing to t4g.xlarge" as though it were a standing prohibition on instance type. It is narrower than that: both ADRs say the SAME sentence, that overlap is capped one-in/one-out "guarded by a memory-pressure alarm, so the transient 2x rebar-mcp never forces the t4g.large up to t4g.xlarge". That is MEMORY-scoped and specific to MCP DEPLOY OVERLAP. Neither ADR says anything about root volume size, and neither is a general bar on resizing the host. The ADR therefore declines the resize ON ITS OWN MERITS (an unbounded generator fills any volume) and records the t4g.large constraint separately WITH its exact scope. My stronger framing should not be repeated.

4. src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py (not src/rebar/reviewbot/); line 381 confirmed.

## TWO findings that strengthen the design and change S6's shape

- **A fast-fail admission seam ALREADY EXISTS.** src/rebar/review_bot/low_disk.py plus janitor.py's ensure_min_free_space / SnapshotLowDiskError / DEFAULT_MIN_FREE_GIB already REFUSE before cloning, on a free-space floor. So S6 should extend that seam with a second term (a concurrency counter) rather than introducing a parallel admission mechanism. This materially simplifies S6 and avoids a new mechanism the ratchet would count.
- **REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR already parameterises the snapshot store's base dir**, so Option C (dedicated gate-scratch volume) is largely CONFIG, not code.
- Also: the per-generator-alarm constraint is an argument from repo history, not preference — rebar-root-disk-pressure already existed at 85% with treat_missing_data=breaching (bug ac14, after incident 2731) and did NOT prevent 3276, because it can only say "root disk high" and never names the saturated generator.

## ADR decision summary (7 decisions)

(1) per-accumulator hard caps at each consumer's native GC; (2) every capped generator carries its own alarm, demoting root-disk-pressure to backstop; (3) gate scratch on a dedicated EBS volume; (4) root stays 60 GiB as headroom not fix; (5) bounded concurrency with FAST-FAIL admission — one shared counter for plan-review and completion-verifier, refusal not queueing, and on the review-bot path it follows ADR 0069's retryable-deferral shape and MAY NEVER BECOME AN LLM-Review -1; (6) caps are measured defaults settable via [snapshot]/REBAR_GATE_* and terraform vars, never constants; (7) host sizing not reopened.

Load-bearing argument, built as a symmetry: prune could not reach 6.5 GB of orphaned overlay2 (~1.06 GB ceiling vs a 29 GB problem), and a watermark GC cannot reach bytes held open by live readers. Both reclaimers pointed at structurally unreachable bytes. Bounded concurrency is therefore a PRECONDITION for the caps, not an addition to them.

## Consequence noted for later: the root_disk_pressure alarm DESCRIPTION still says "The box's 30G ROOT disk" while var.root_volume_size_gb is 60. Cosmetic but misleading during an incident.

NEXT ACTION: re-run review-plan on S0 now the 0110->0111 correction has landed in the ticket, then claim S0 and commit the drafted ADR.
